Cyber Attack Disrupts Azerbaijan’s Industrial Intermediate Prod Firms, Halting Operations and Forcing Shutdowns

BAKU, June 14 – A large-scale cyber attack targeting Azerbaijan’s Industrial Intermediate Prod sector has forced several manufacturers to halt operations, with firms across the country reporting ransomware infections that have crippled IT systems and disrupted plant activity.

According to the Azerbaijan Industrial Intermediate Producers Union, at least eight firms in Sumgait, Mingachevir, and Ganja reported sudden interruptions late Wednesday after malicious software encrypted critical data on production servers. The industry group said the attack, believed to be ransomware, is ongoing and has rendered core manufacturing, inventory, and safety systems inaccessible.

"This is an unprecedented situation for our sector," said Arif Zeynalov, president of the union, in a statement. "Our members cannot access digital controls for their processing lines, and production has come to a complete standstill at several sites. We are working with national authorities and independent cybersecurity experts to contain the spread and recover operations."

Employees at the affected plants were told not to report for shifts Thursday and Friday, union officials said, as management teams assess the extent of the breach and attempt to restore backup systems. "Until we are certain the threat is neutralized, we cannot risk restarting production lines or allowing workers into potentially compromised environments," Zeynalov added.

A spokesperson for Prodinvest, one of the impacted firms, said its three facilities in the Sumgait industrial zone had been forced offline since early Thursday morning. "We are unable to access any production data or operate machinery safely," the spokesperson said. "Our IT and security teams are working around the clock, but we do not yet have a timeline for resuming normal operations."

The government’s National Cybersecurity Center confirmed it was coordinating with affected companies and law enforcement agencies. In a brief statement, the center advised all firms in the sector to disconnect non-essential systems and avoid opening suspicious emails or attachments.

Analysts say the attack highlights vulnerabilities in the sector’s digital infrastructure. "Many Industrial Intermediate Prod companies have modernized rapidly but often lack robust cybersecurity protocols," said Leyla Abbasova, a Baku-based industrial risk consultant. "This incident will likely prompt a sector-wide review of digital risk management."

The full scale of disruption remains unclear, but industry officials warned that continued downtime could have lasting effects for workers and production targets. "We are in uncharted territory," Zeynalov said. "Our immediate goal is to secure our systems and get our people safely back to work."
